title: ProfileFunctionImpl reads EPS.originalEnd directly for remaining-time display, producing garbage duration (e.g. "32399999998h")
body:
# Widget / overview "remaining time" shows absurd duration (e.g. "32399999998h") for a running temporary ProfileSwitch

## Where

`implementation/src/main/kotlin/app/aaps/implementation/profile/ProfileFunctionImpl.kt`,
`getProfileName()`:

```kotlin
if (showRemainingTime && profileSwitch.originalDuration != 0L) {
    profileName += dateUtil.untilString(profileSwitch.originalEnd, rh)
}
```

This is used by both the home-screen widget (`Widget.kt` → `updateProfile()`) and the Overview
ribbon (`OverviewFragment.kt`) via `ProfileFunction.getProfileNameWithRemainingTime()`.

## What happens

`dateUtil.untilString(profileSwitch.originalEnd, rh)` treats `originalEnd` as an absolute epoch
timestamp and subtracts `now()` from it. When the stored `originalEnd` value on a given EPS record
doesn't actually match `timestamp + originalDuration`, the resulting delta is nonsensical and gets
rendered as something like `(32399999998ч 11')` instead of a sane duration.

## Why this happens

`EPS.originalEnd` (`core/data/src/main/kotlin/app/aaps/core/data/model/EPS.kt`) and
`EffectiveProfileSwitch.originalEnd` (`database/impl/.../entities/EffectiveProfileSwitch.kt`) are
both explicitly documented as:

```kotlin
var originalEnd: Long, // not used (calculated from duration)
```

Every other consumer of this field in the codebase already treats it as unreliable and derives the
real end time from `timestamp + originalDuration` instead:

- `ProfileSwitchExpiryScheduler.kt` (doc comment): *"the EffectiveProfileSwitch query selects the
  latest EPS by timestamp and ignores `originalEnd`"* — it schedules the revert-to-base event off
  `timestamp + duration`, not off `originalEnd`.
- `SceneExecutor.kt` (comment): *"...and ignores originalEnd, so the base profile only resumes once
  a NEW base-profile EPS exists."*

`ProfileFunctionImpl.getProfileName()` is the one place left that still reads `originalEnd`
directly for display purposes, contradicting the documented contract of the field.

## How the stale value gets there

`originalEnd` is only guaranteed correct at the moment of local creation
(`CommandQueueImplementation.kt`: `originalEnd = it.end` where `PS.end = timestamp + duration`).
On an **AAPSCLIENT / follower** setup, the EPS record is never created locally — it's synced verbatim
from Nightscout (`EffectiveProfileSwitchExtension.kt` / `NsIncomingDataProcessor.kt`), so whatever
`originalEnd` value was serialized to NS at creation time is trusted as-is, with no re-derivation
from `timestamp + duration` and no sanity bound. Any divergence between the two (stale historical
NS record, a different NS-writing client with a different convention, clock skew at write time,
etc.) surfaces directly as garbage in the UI, since nothing downstream re-derives or clamps it.

## Suggested fix

```kotlin
if (showRemainingTime && profileSwitch.originalDuration != 0L) {
    profileName += dateUtil.untilString(profileSwitch.timestamp + profileSwitch.originalDuration, rh)
}
```

This makes the display consistent with how `ProfileSwitchExpiryScheduler` and `SceneExecutor`
already treat this field, and removes the dependency on a field the data model itself documents as
unused.

## Confirmed present on

- `original/dev` @ `9df0b1bd4e` ("fix ProfileHelper and EPS caching")
- `original/dev3` @ `ab1f6040cc` ("Cleanup")

## Repro

Observed on a fork build (AAPSCLIENT/follower widget) while a temporary ProfileSwitch (`120%`,
fixed duration) was active: the widget's active-profile line showed
`#26 <profile name> (120%)(32399999998ч 11')` instead of a plausible remaining duration.

## Addendum: not AAPSCLIENT-specific

Dug a bit deeper into the sync path — this is **not limited to AAPSCLIENT/follower setups**. The
defective read in `ProfileFunctionImpl.getProfileName()` has no `config.AAPSCLIENT` guard at all, so
it's the exact same code path on a regular master (pump-owning) install.

The reason it's *easier* to trigger on AAPSCLIENT is that a follower never creates EPS records
locally — `CommandQueueImplementation`'s `EventProfileSwitchChanged` handler (which is the only
place that sets `originalEnd = it.end`, i.e. correctly, at creation time) is short-circuited with
`if (config.AAPSCLIENT) return@subscribe`. So 100% of a follower's EPS data comes from Nightscout
verbatim, `originalEnd` included, with nothing re-deriving or sanity-checking it.

A **master** install normally keeps its own EPS records self-consistent (locally created with a
correct `originalEnd`), and the inbound-sync transaction
(`SyncNsEffectiveProfileSwitchTransaction`) never overwrites an existing local record's fields —
on nsId match it only allows invalidation, on timestamp match without an nsId it only backfills the
nsId. So master doesn't corrupt its *own* records via sync.

However, master still **inserts brand-new EPS records sourced from Nightscout** (with whatever
`originalEnd` NS provided, unvalidated) whenever:

- `NsClientAcceptProfileSwitch` is enabled (`NsIncomingDataProcessor.kt`) — a commonly-enabled
  setting for accepting profile switches made via other clients / the NS web UI, or
- a full resync happens (`doFullSync`, e.g. after reinstall).

In either case, a mismatched/stale `originalEnd` on that inbound record (different uploading
client, historical NS data, clock skew at original write time, etc.) will render the same garbage
duration on a *regular* AAPS install, not just on a follower.

So the fix (deriving the end time from `timestamp + originalDuration` instead of trusting the
stored `originalEnd`) is warranted for master builds too, not just AAPSCL

Update: the display fallback in #4987 / #4988 (deriving the remaining-time text from `timestamp + originalDuration` instead of trusting `originalEnd`) did correct the rendering on the home-screen widget. But the Overview status-screen ribbon — which reads the exact same `ProfileFunction.getProfileNameWithRemainingTime()` — kept showing the same kind of nonsensical duration on a later, newly-created instance of the same recurring profile switch. That's because that record's `originalDuration` was itself already corrupted at the source; a display-layer fix can't repair data that's wrong going in.

Thanks @MilosKozak for finding and fixing the actual root cause directly (`52056ebeb4` / `6bdbf1498`, `ProfileSwitchExtension.kt`: `originalDuration` vs `duration` when parsing legacy NSClientV3 `ProfileSwitch` documents). That's a different, more specific bug than what I originally described here — it explains *why* the duration gets corrupted in the first place, not just how it renders once corrupted.

I've ported that commit onto our branch alongside the display fallback and will test it today against the actual recurring automation rule that's been producing these corrupted switches, to confirm new occurrences parse correctly going forward.

Confirmed fixed: after building and installing with @MilosKozak's fix (`52056ebeb4` / `6bdbf1498`), the recurring automation rule that was producing corrupted `ProfileSwitch` documents no longer triggers the nonsensical duration — new occurrences render correctly, on both the widget and the Overview status ribbon. Problem is gone. Thanks again for tracking down the actual root cause.
